title: Insight 1: Several 'easy' rides breached the Zone 1 ceiling
description: Rides on Oct 27, Nov 1, Nov 5, Nov 6, and Nov 8 averaged 145–158 bpm, which sits in Zone 2 (139–159 bpm) rather than the intended easy Zone 1 (<139 bpm). Keeping truly easy days below 139 bpm will improve recovery and aerobic base.

title: Insight 2: Nov 6 ride had a notable vertical spike
description: The 47 km ride on Nov 6 packed 433 m of climbing (9.2 m/km), nearly double the 4–5 m/km of other rides. That extra gravity load explains the higher avg HR (148 bpm) and NP (180 W) despite similar distance.

title: Insight 3: Seven rides in 15 days creates tight recovery windows
description: Riding every 2 days on average (including back-to-back days Nov 5–6 and Nov 8–10) leaves little room for adaptation. Consider inserting a full rest day or a very short spin after two consecutive ride days.

title: Insight 4: Cycling progression has plateaued at VO2max 49
description: Cycling VO2max has held at 49.0 since Oct 23 despite consistent riding. Distance and intensity haven't progressively increased; adding a weekly longer ride (2.5–3 h) or structured intervals can nudge the next gain.

title: Insight 5: HR and power zones are reasonably aligned
description: Zone 2 HR (139–159 bpm) corresponds well to Zone 2 power (112–152 W) — your typical rides average 145–152 bpm and 130–150 W. No urgent need to retest thresholds unless feel changes.

title: Insight 6: Training is mostly moderate — missing polarization
description: Almost all ride time falls in Zone 2 (moderate), with minimal Zone 1 (<139 bpm) recovery time and no dedicated Zone 4/5 intervals. Aim for ~80% of time in Zone 1, ~20% in Zone 4+ to boost fitness without fatigue.

title: Insight 7: Sleep and HRV dip on Nov 10 signals recovery debt
description: Only 4 h 42 min sleep, HRV 64 ms (week low), and readiness 80 despite low stress (23) suggest accumulated fatigue. Prioritize 7+ h sleep tonight and consider an easy spin or rest tomorrow.

title: Insight 8: Strong neuromuscular power shown in short bursts
description: 10-second peaks hit 981 W (Nov 5) and 583 W (Oct 27), indicating good sprint capacity. Maintain this with occasional 10–15 sec all-out sprints or off-bike strength work (e.g., plyometrics, heavy squats).

title: Insight 9: VO2max boost — add structured interval sessions
description: To lift VO2max above 49, include 1–2 weekly sessions like 4×4 min at 105–110% FTP (213–223 W) with 4 min easy recovery, or 5×3 min at 115% FTP. Do these on fresh legs after a rest day.

title: Insight 10: FTP estimate (203 W) likely low — schedule a test
description: Current FTP derives from 95% of a 20-min effort (214 W) on Oct 25; Garmin's old 271 W is stale. A fresh 20-min test or ramp test will set accurate zones and track true progress.
